impact: Exact corrected protocol the re-spec drafts must encode. (1) Ordering: any unlink of the control-socket pathname happens ONLY while holding the port singleton, and only after a probe finds no live endpoint — startup order fixed by the T-008 handover: validate write-once token → validate write-once allocation → acquire port → probe unix socket → reclaim only confirmed-stale → bind socket → serve; the stop sequence's final 'remove only a verified-stale socket' step inherits the same holding-the-singleton rule. (2) Honest contract, written into both T-011 and T-015: this guarantees a live COOPERATING spendbar instance's socket is never unlinked (all spendbar probe/unlink activity is serialized by the singleton), and it does NOT close the TOCTOU against an unrelated or hostile same-UID process binding the pathname between probe and unlink. (3) The draft must choose and encode one of the issue's two options: (a) per-instance socket pathname published through the write-once allocation, so no pathname is ever reused and nothing is ever deleted on the strength of an earlier observation — and then add an adversarial test with a competing binder in the probe/unlink window, not only cooperative failure injection; or (b) keep the fixed pathname + probe-then-unlink-under-singleton, and explicitly accept and document the residual same-UID denial-of-service (refuse-to-start/diagnose, never fight). (4) Either way, the unconditional 'a live server's socket must never be unlinked' wording in T-011 criterion 3 (and T-015 criterion 3's implied equivalent) must be deleted or narrowed to the cooperating-instance guarantee — as written it cannot be met by any implementation of the specified procedure. (5) The re-spec must not cite T-008 as having validated any stale-socket probe: T-008 criterion 5 records that clause as an explicit gap owned by T-011.
resolution: Fixed by the v0.2/v0.3 ticket re-spec applied 2026-08-02: T-011 and T-015 no longer specify probe-then-unlink: the service unlinks only its own socket during graceful shutdown; crash-leftover reclamation follows the corrected confirmed-stale protocol under the singleton, with the narrows-but-does-not-close honesty preserved. The full verified requirements record is preserved in this issue's impact field.
title: T-011 and T-015 specify probe-then-unlink for stale sockets, which is a TOCTOU that can delete a live server's socket
